text:
Pavel Zacha has 15 points in 19 games for Boston, seven of them on the power play, and he is doing it while his name sits in trade columns. The Hockey Writers argued on Nov. 7 that the Bruins should move him now for top value, and Causeway Crowd ran an analyst's case that unloading him might be easier than people think. That is the backdrop for a 29-year-old who is playing over 20 minutes a night lately.

The production is a little ahead of the process. His own shots are worth 5.14 expected goals (the quality of his chances) and he has five goals, so his finishing is honest. The points come from teammates: the team is scoring 4.41 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of luck rarely holds.

What to watch: he is still the player Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked last season, carrying the puck in on 60% of entries and getting 6.6 home-plate chances per 60. Five of his last ten games were losses, and how the Bruins' week goes may decide whether the trade talk gets louder.
headline: Pavel Zacha, producing while the rumors swirl
